Create one original promotional asset for Peeplet, a cozy collectible pet game where players mint an egg, care for their Peeplet, and discover different rarities as the game grows.

Website reference: https://peeplet.com/

The asset can be:

A short video
A meme
A graphic
A mini review
A screenshot-based creative
A short written promo concept

Focus on one of these angles:

Mint an egg → care for your pet
Every Peeplet can have different rarity
Cute pet game meets collectibles
New things to discover as the game grows
Why the concept feels fun or nostalgic

Requirements:

Must be original.
Must clearly mention or show Peeplet.
Must include the Peeplet website as reference.
No fake engagement, bot content, copied posts, spam, or mass tagging.
No promises of profit, financial return, or NFT value.
No minors, nudity, violence, doxxing, harassment, or misleading AI-generated “proof.”

Submit the created content file, image, text, or link as proof.

Success means the content feels authentic, fun, and easy to understand for someone seeing Peeplet for the first time.

I, EnHeng, am putting this bounty on the table: anyone who can create a real, legal, verifiable path for me to join a SpaceX or Starship related crewed spaceflight mission — the bounty is yours.

that's exactly why this bounty exists.

At the very least, on day 8, I want the entire internet to look at this bounty and say: "Wait, what? EnHeng went to space??"

The only payout condition

The full bounty goes to one party only: whoever makes the official crew list announcement happen. Payment is released only after I complete the mission and return safely to Earth.

ALL three of the following must be true:

1. I (EnHeng) am named on the crew list of a specific crewed mission, announced by SpaceX, NASA, or an official space agency — only spacex.com, nasa.gov, @SpaceX, or the agency's verified site/account counts. No other source qualifies: no media reports, no companies, no emails, no DMs, no middlemen.
2. The mission is a real, publicly listed crewed mission, and the crew list is verifiable by anyone.
3. I fly that same mission, livestream the journey to space and the landing, and return safely to Earth.

No stage payments. No partial rewards. No progress bonuses.

What does not count: AI-generated anything, edited screenshots, private DMs, verbal promises, second-hand reports, "I know a guy", or anything only you can verify.

If a qualifying official crew list announcement (items 1+2) lands within the 7-day window, the bounty stays locked until the mission completes. If not, the bounty closes on day 8 — unallocated funds are expected to be returned per the platform's rules and mechanics, and I will publish a transparency report listing every submission received and how it was evaluated.

Who can't claim: me, my team, my family, anyone I've paid in the last 12 months, and any wallet that has received funds from my wallet in the last 30 days. Must be 18+, not located in a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction, and not on the OFAC SDN or any equivalent sanctions list.

Legal, short version: this is a public reward offer — not employment, not an investment, not a security. You participate at your own cost and risk. My judgment on verification is final, subject to the platform's rules and dispute resolution process.

Day 8: see you in the transparency report.

— EnHeng

April the Giraffe, a reticulated giraffe at Animal Adventure Park in New York, became a worldwide viral sensation in 2017 when over 232 million people watched the YouTube live stream of her pregnancy and labor. April, who died in 2021 at age 20, brought massive attention to giraffe conservation.  Other notable giraffes include: Zarafa (1824–1845): A famous female Nubian giraffe sent from Egypt to France, the first seen in Europe in over 300 years. Misha: A Perth Zoo giraffe known from the iconic "The Kiss" photograph with her calf. Geoffrey: The animated mascot for Toys "R" Us. Tajiri: April's calf, whose birth was the subject of the 2017 viral event.  This video shows the moment April the Giraffe finally gave birth: Related video thumbnail 01:01 BBC World Service Facebook • Apr 16, 2017 April's fame was propelled by a live-streamed, months-long wait for her calf, bringing international attention to Animal Adventure Park. Her story and subsequent death from arthritis in 2021 was widely covered by news outlets like NBC New York.  Remembering April the Giraffe: It was four years ago today when April the Giraffe sadly passed away after suffering from arthritis—just sixteen days before her 21st birthday. April gained ENORMOUS internet fame in April of 2017 while pregnant with her baby, Tajiri. The folks at Animal Adventure Park in Harpursville, NY (Broome County) had the good sense to have a live camera feed installed during her labor—April went full viral and when all was finished, the YouTube feed amassed an astounding 232 million views. Tajiri remains at Animal Adventure Park—they open for the season on April 22nd. These are captures I took when I visited April the Giraffe back in 2018.
